source.title: On reconstruction of task context after interruption
source.venue: Proceedings of the SIGCHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI 2010)

confidence_rationale: Directly measures and models the cost the interruption_snapshot exists to avoid: after an interruption, resuming a task requires re-encoding ('reconstructing') context to identify the next step, and this reconstruction cost (resumption lag) is what a preserved snapshot is architecturally meant to short-circuit. The finding that interruption timing relative to subtask boundaries changes the cost is a specific, actionable design input for MECH-524's trigger.
failure_signatures: Interruptions landing mid-subtask (mid-CEM-rollout, in REE terms) cost more to reconstruct/resume from than interruptions landing at a natural subtask boundary; a re-seeding trigger that treats all interruption points as equivalent will under-predict resumption cost for mid-rollout interruptions and may need the snapshot to carry more of the in-progress CEM state precisely when the interruption is least boundary-aligned.

Without a preserved context, the reconstruction process itself consumes time and attention that could otherwise go toward resuming actual task progress -- an REE agent lacking an interruption_snapshot pays an analogous reconstruction tax even after MECH-293/MECH-285 correctly re-flag the parked goal as worth resuming.

mapping.source_claim_statement: After an interruption, resuming a primary task requires re-encoding information necessary to identify what step comes next -- a reconstruction process that takes measurable time (resumption lag, the interval between finishing the secondary/interrupting task and resuming productive primary-task action). Reconstruction is faster, and resumption lag shorter, when the interruption occurs at a natural subtask boundary than when it lands mid-subtask, because subtask completion leaves less in-progress context that needs to be re-derived.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the most direct grounding for why MECH-524 proposes a richer interruption_snapshot (z_world + z_self + z_goal + CEM stage + rule-arbitration weights + what-was-attempted) rather than relying on SD-039's simpler goal-snapshot payload: the snapshot's entire purpose is to make the reconstruction step Salvucci measures unnecessary, by having the in-progress context already captured rather than re-derived from scratch. The boundary-timing finding is a concrete, testable design input: the trigger and snapshot mechanism should be expected to matter MORE (produce a larger resumption-lag reduction) for interruptions that land mid-CEM-rollout than for ones that land at a clean rule-arbitration boundary, since the latter have less in-progress context to lose in the first place.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Human office/procedural-editing task domain (a text/photo editing task interrupted by a secondary task) modeled via a production-system cognitive architecture, not an embodied agent with a continuous world model and CEM-based planning; 'reconstruction' here is re-deriving declarative task state (what step am I on), which is a looser analogue of re-priming a structured latent snapshot. The boundary-timing effect is measured in a domain with clean, human-recognizable subtask boundaries -- REE's CEM-stage boundaries may not be similarly clean, and that mapping is untested.
mapping.source_context: Cognitive-architecture model plus behavioral timing data from a dual-task paradigm: a primary procedural task interrupted by a secondary task at controlled points, measuring resumption lag as a function of interruption timing relative to subtask structure.

confidence_components.notes: Short CHI paper (4 pages) rather than a full journal article, but from a well-established threaded-cognition research program with a track record of empirically validated cognitive models. Mapping fidelity is high at the design-rationale level (this is literally the cost the snapshot is built to avoid); transfer risk from the HCI/office-task domain to REE's embodied continuous-control setting is a real, stated caveat.
